title: Identification and molecular characterization of a metagenome-derived L-lysine decarboxylase gene
author: Jie Deng
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jdaci2e
materials: Section 2: The extraction of plasmid DNA.

steps.title: Extract metagenomic DNA from soil
steps.instruction: Isolate DNA from 5 g of subtropical soil using a modified Zhou and Bürgmann method with three extraction cycles, chloroform/isoamyl extraction, isopropanol precipitation, ethanol washes and TE resuspension.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 5 g of soil into a tube and add 13.6 mL of DNA extraction buffer (100 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 100 mM EDTA, 100 mM NaH₂PO₄, 1.5 M NaCl, 1 % CTAB). Mix thoroughly.
Freeze the mixture at –80 °C for 30 min, then thaw in a 65 °C water bath until completely melted.
Add SDS (20 % stock) to reach a final concentration of 1 % (v/v) and add proteinase K to a final concentration of 100 µg mL⁻¹. Incubate at 65 °C for 2 h, vortexing up‑and‑down every 15 min.
Centrifuge at 5,000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature; transfer the supernatant to a new tube.

Repeat the extraction two more times: add 4.5 mL fresh extraction buffer to the remaining soil pellet, freeze at –80 °C for 10 min, thaw in a 65 °C water bath, add SDS (20 % stock) to 1 % final and proteinase K to 100 µg mL⁻¹, incubate at 65 °C for 10 min, then centrifuge as above and collect the supernatant.

Combine the three supernatants and add an equal volume of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1, v/v). Mix gently and centrifuge at 5,000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature. Transfer the aqueous (upper) phase to a fresh tube.
Add 0.6 vol of isopropanol to the aqueous phase, mix, and let the DNA precipitate at room temperature for 1 h.
Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm for 20 min at room temperature. Discard the supernatant and wash the pellet twice with cold 70 % ethanol.
Dry the pellet by vacuum concentration until all ethanol has evaporated, then dissolve the DNA in TE buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA). Store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Perform alkaline lysis plasmid extraction
steps.instruction: Prepare alkaline lysis solutions I‑III and extract plasmid DNA from bacterial cells using alkaline lysis followed by phenol‑chloroform purification.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Solution I: 50 mM glucose, 25 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0), 10 mM EDTA (pH 8.0).
Prepare Solution II: 0.2 M NaOH, 1 % SDS.
Prepare Solution III: 5 M potassium acetate, acetic acid, adjust to pH 4.8.
Resuspend harvested bacterial cells in Solution I, add Solution II, mix gently, then add Solution III to neutralize. Mix briefly.
Extract the lysate with an equal volume of phenol‑chloroform (25:24, v/v), vortex, and centrifuge to separate phases.
Recover the aqueous phase and proceed with downstream plasmid purification as described in the referenced alkaline‑lysis miniprep protocol.

steps.title: Derivatize 1,5-pentanediamine with dansyl chloride
steps.instruction: Convert 1,5‑pentanediamine to its dansyl derivative for HPLC analysis.

substeps.instruction: Place 0.1 mL of the 1,5‑pentanediamine standard in a micro‑tube.
Add 20 µL of 2 M NaOH and 30 µL of saturated NaHCO₃ solution; mix briefly.
Add 200 µL of dansyl chloride solution (10 mg mL⁻¹) and incubate at 60 °C for 30 min.
Add 100 µL of 25 % NH₄OH to quench excess dansyl chloride.
Adjust the final volume to 2 mL with acetonitrile.
Filter the solution through a 0.2 µm syringe filter before analysis.

steps.title: Assay L-lysine decarboxylase activity (TNBS)
steps.instruction: Measure LDC activity spectrophotometrically using the TNBS assay based on differential solubility of reaction products.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the reaction mixture containing 0.1 mM pyridoxal‑5′‑phosphate (PLP), 2 mM L‑lysine·HCl, 3 µg recombinant LDC protein, and 0.2 M Na₂HPO₄/0.1 M citric acid buffer (pH 6.5). Incubate under the desired assay conditions (reaction time not specified in the source).
Terminate the reaction by adding 250 µL of 1 M K₂CO₃.
Add 200 µL of 9.6 mM TNBS solution, then incubate at 40 °C for 5 min.
Add 1 mL of toluene and vortex at maximum speed for 1 min to extract the TNP‑pentanediamine product.
Centrifuge the mixture at 4,000 rpm for 15 min to separate the toluene layer.
Measure the absorbance of the aqueous layer at 340 nm; the absorbance is proportional to L‑lysine decarboxylase activity.
